recap.title: Skeleton first, data second

recap.body: After a short bounded wait the screen draws from localStorage; the cloud sync comes after.

recap.body: bootApp guards itself, so a second auth event can't start the app twice.

steps.title: The page skeleton is built first.
steps.why: Before anyone is signed in, index.js builds the whole page and attaches it to the body.

steps.title: component() makes the empty layout.
steps.why: Nav bar, sidebar, list and footer are created here, still with no projects in them.

steps.title: Signed in? Boot. Otherwise, offline or the gate.
steps.why: A saved session boots the app. Without one, a device that chose offline boots into local mode; everyone else gets the gate.

steps.title: bootApp paints after a short bounded wait.
steps.why: The cloud probe (FIRST_RUN_PROBE_TIMEOUT_MS) and target warm-up (BOOT_TARGETS_WAIT_MS) are capped; then this device's copy draws.

steps.title: restoreFromStorage draws the sidebar and list.
steps.why: One sidebar row per project, then the selected project's todos in the main list.

steps.title: Then sync: migrate, hydrate, subscribe.
steps.why: Upload old local data once, pull everything from Supabase, then listen for live changes.

recap.title: The watchdog stands down early
recap.body: markAppBooted runs as soon as the shell exists, before any data is drawn.

recap.title: The render step reports its own failure
recap.body: A throw in restoreFromStorage calls reportBootFailure and skips the sync pipeline.

recap.title: Only a pre-paint failure escalates
recap.body: The terminal catch checks rendered; a failed sync after the paint stays a warning.

recap.title: The page owns the recovery
recap.body: Quiet reload, then a full cache bust, then a Reload prompt.

steps.title: bootApp latches, then signals the boot.

steps.title: markAppBooted stands the watchdog down.
steps.why: It sets the success flag, resets the recovery count and clears the overlay, before any data is pulled [src: index.js:81].

steps.title: The render waits on two bounded steps.
steps.why: The cloud probe and the targets warm-up each resolve by their timeout, so neither can hold the paint for long.

steps.title: A throw in the render step is caught here.
steps.why: The shell is up but empty. It is reported, then returned, so the sync pipeline never runs [src: index.js:160].

steps.title: reportBootFailure calls the page's hook.
steps.why: The watchdog already stood down, so this hands the failure back to its reload ladder [src: index.js:95].

steps.title: Only a failure before the paint escalates.
steps.why: A failed sync after the paint stays a warning; escalating it would reload-loop you through an outage [src: index.js:202].

steps.title: A page load tries the network first.
steps.why: Follows opening the app offline: your projects still appear. The page request gives up on the network after four seconds.

steps.title: Then the cached shell, then the precached one.
steps.why: With no shell in the runtime cache yet, the precached index.html still boots the app [src: sw.js:40].

steps.title: The build's files come from the precache.
steps.why: Bundles and assets are served from cache, and their URLs change per build, so a hit is always the right one [src: sw.js:27].

steps.title: A failed session probe goes to bootWithoutSession.
steps.why: If the probe itself fails, the sign-in gate renders, or an offline-mode device boots locally [src: index.js:286].

steps.title: bootApp waits out its bounds.
steps.why: Offline, the cloud probe and the targets warm-up end by their timeouts at the latest, then the render step runs.

steps.title: restoreFromStorage paints this device's copy.
steps.why: Projects and tasks come from localStorage, which needs no network.

steps.title: The sync fails and only logs it.
steps.why: The cloud pull cannot complete offline; a rejection lands here as a warning and the painted screen stays as it is.

steps.title: The online event re-syncs on reconnect.
steps.why: The cloud copy is pulled again and live updates are re-subscribed [src: index.js:515].

tours.title: Signing in with an emailed code

recap.title: Two screens, one gate
recap.body: Email first, then the code. Both live inside the full-screen modal auth.js mounts.

recap.title: A code, not a link
recap.body: Entering the code inside the app keeps the session in the app's own storage.

recap.title: The listener boots, not the form
recap.body: verifyCode only reports success. The auth listener in index.js adopts the session and calls bootApp.

recap.title: Booting is latched
recap.body: The session probe and the listener may both call bootApp. Only the first call does anything.

steps.title: No saved session: no boot yet.
steps.why: This tour follows a successful sign-in. The first visit has no session, and you land on the Welcome screen.

steps.title: No offline choice either, so the gate goes up.
steps.why: Only a device that chose offline skips it. Everyone else gets the full-screen sign-in form.

steps.title: The gate covers the page.
steps.why: Any earlier gate is torn down first, then screen 1 renders with an empty email field.

steps.title: Continue asks for a code.
steps.why: The button stays disabled while the request is out. Success swaps in the code screen.

steps.title: Supabase emails a one-time code.
steps.why: Only an existing account gets one. No error means the code is on its way to your inbox.

steps.title: Verify sends the code you typed.
steps.why: On success this screen does nothing more. The auth listener in index.js takes over from here.

steps.title: The code becomes a session.
steps.why: Supabase checks the code and stores the session in the installed app's own storage.

steps.title: The auth listener hears the new session.
steps.why: Supabase announces the sign-in. The listener adopts the session, hides the gate and boots.

steps.title: The session is adopted.
steps.why: This device is marked as using its account. Returning false tells the listener to boot here.

steps.title: bootApp runs, once.
steps.why: The latch makes any later call a no-op. The app paints locally, then syncs, as the first chapter showed.

tours.title: When the email or code is refused

recap.title: Three ways sendCode says no
recap.body: No account for that email, too many tries, or couldn't send: each is a short message on screen 1.

recap.title: No sign-ups from the gate
recap.body: shouldCreateUser: false means an unknown email fails instead of creating an account.

recap.title: Retries stay on their screen
recap.body: A refused email or code re-enables the button where you are. Nothing navigates away.

recap.title: Resend waits 60 seconds
recap.body: The countdown matches Supabase's per-address limit and restarts on every resend.

steps.title: An empty email never leaves the form.
steps.why: This tour follows the refusals. The first is local: no address, no request, just a message.

steps.title: The gate never creates an account.
steps.why: Sign-ups are closed. An unknown address fails instead of quietly making a new user [src: auth.js:383].

match: return { ok: false, message: 'Too many tries — wait a moment' };
steps.title: Too many requests: wait a moment.
steps.why: Supabase rate-limits codes per address. A 429 or a rate hint reads as a calm wait message.

match: return { ok: false, message: 'No account for that email' };
steps.title: Unknown address: no account.
steps.why: The sign-ups-disabled error is named plainly, and reads as a missing account rather than a fault.

match: return { ok: false, message: "Couldn't send code — try again" };
steps.title: Anything else, or no network: try again.
steps.why: Any other error, and a request that never got an answer, share one generic message.

steps.title: A refusal re-enables Continue.
steps.why: You stay on screen 1 with sendCode's message under the field. Fixing the address and retrying happens here.

match: return { ok: false, message: "That code didn't work — check it or resend" };
steps.title: A wrong or expired code is refused.
steps.why: Any verify error means the code didn't match. The message points you at checking it or resending.

steps.title: The code screen lets you try again.
steps.why: Verify re-enables and focus returns to the code field. The retry happens on this screen.

steps.title: Resend restarts the wait and sends again.
steps.why: The countdown restarts at once. A rate-limit refusal still shows its message under the buttons.

steps.title: Resend waits out a 60-second window.
steps.why: Supabase allows one code per address a minute; a shorter wait would make each resend fail [src: auth.js:35].

tours.title: Using the app offline, then signing in later

recap.title: Offline is one stored choice

recap.title: Offline boots with no user

recap.body: Mount sites and the stylesheet both hide Worker and pipeline surfaces when it is false.

recap.title: Signing in later reloads
recap.body: A session on an offline shell flips the mode to account and reloads; the signed-in boot uploads your data.

steps.title: The gate's second door: use offline.
steps.why: This tour follows a visitor with no account. One tap stores the choice, hides the gate and boots.

steps.title: The choice is saved and stamped on the page.
steps.why: Stored under todoapp_accessMode, and set on the html element, where the stylesheet hides pipeline surfaces.

steps.title: bootLocalMode runs a boot index.js lent it.
steps.why: auth.js can't import the entry module, and index.js registers its boot here instead [src: accessMode.js:129].

steps.title: That boot is bootApp with no user.
steps.why: A shell that already booted ignores it, since bootApp is latched.

steps.title: No user: paint locally, then stop.
steps.why: The ghost is not mounted offline, and with no user bootApp returns before bootSyncPipeline runs.

steps.title: After a reload, the gate is skipped.
steps.why: With no session but the offline choice stored, the next load boots straight into local mode.

steps.title: Settings offers Sign in instead of Sign out.
steps.why: Offline, the Account row reopens the same gate. Signing in then follows the code tour's path.

steps.title: A session on an offline shell means a reload.
steps.why: The running page was built offline, and every surface must remount signed in [src: index.js:250].

steps.title: Flip to account, then reload.
steps.why: bootApp is latched and cannot remount in place; the signed-in boot after the reload migrates offline data up.

recap.title: Wipe, then sign out
recap.body: wipeLocalUserDataOnSignOut runs while the session still exists, then Supabase ends it.

recap.title: The listener does the teardown
recap.body: The auth listener's no-session branch empties listLogic, unmounts the ghost and shows the gate.

recap.title: Device prefs survive
recap.body: Only user data is removed. Theme, sidebar width and other preferences stay on the device.

recap.title: Offline mode is untouched
recap.body: With no session to lose, a local-mode device skips the teardown.

steps.title: Sign out starts in Settings.
steps.why: This tour follows signing out (mobile's Settings has the same row). The device is wiped, then the session ends.

steps.title: This device's cached data is removed.
steps.why: It runs while the session still exists, to read the user id. Theme and other device prefs stay.

steps.title: The listener hears the session end.
steps.why: Its no-session branch runs. An offline device has no session to lose and returns here.

steps.title: listLogic is told to forget.
steps.why: The data model is emptied before the gate returns, and the next person sees none of it.

steps.title: Realtime closes and memory empties.
steps.why: No more live changes arrive, and the in-memory projects and their cached copy are cleared.

steps.title: The ghost is unmounted.
steps.why: A possessed sheet is handed back first. Signed out, the ghost can't be clicked or talk.

steps.title: The gate goes back up.
steps.why: The page behind stays built, now empty and covered by the sign-in form.

recap.title: One shared client

recap.title: Missing keys never crash
recap.body: Without build-time keys a stub client answers with empty data.

recap.title: Email codes, no passwords
recap.body: sendCode emails a one-time code. verifyCode turns it into a session.

recap.title: The session gates every write
recap.body: persistMutation and hydrate both stop when nobody is signed in.

steps.title: One client, built from build-time keys.
steps.why: Webpack bakes the URL and public key in. The session is saved and refreshed for you.

steps.title: No keys? A stub keeps the app running.
steps.why: It answers every call with empty data, so a local build still opens, signed out.

match: return { ok: false, message: 'No account for that email' };
steps.title: Sign-in starts with an emailed code.
steps.why: Only existing accounts get one. Errors become short messages for the form.

steps.title: The code is swapped for a session.
steps.why: Supabase checks the code. On success the client now holds a signed-in session.

steps.title: Auth changes boot the app or tear it down.
steps.why: A new session hides the modal and boots. Signing out clears data and shows it again.

steps.title: Every write checks the session first.
steps.why: Projects carry your user_id. Todos don't: their access is checked through their project.

steps.title: Hydrate reads everything back.
steps.why: Your projects, then all todos you can see. The database only returns rows you own.

tours.title: What a first sign-in does to this device's data

recap.title: Ask the cloud before onboarding
recap.body: A user with cloud projects skips the sample project and the tour.

recap.title: Migration runs once per user
recap.body: A marker in localStorage records that this device already uploaded.

recap.title: Cloud wins when it has data
recap.body: Local data only uploads into an empty account.

recap.title: Sign-out wipes this device
recap.body: Local projects and the marker go, so the next user starts clean.

steps.title: Boot first asks: do you already have data?
steps.why: The answer decides onboarding, and is passed on so the migration needn't ask again.

steps.title: Existing users skip the welcome.
steps.why: Cloud projects found? Onboarding is marked done. A timeout stops a slow check blocking the page.

steps.title: The probe fetches one project id.
steps.why: One row is enough to know. It returns null on errors, meaning 'couldn't tell'.

steps.title: Local data moves up once per user.
steps.why: Only into an empty account. The marker is set afterwards, so it never runs twice.

steps.title: Each project goes up, then its todos.
steps.why: Parents first, so every todo has a project to belong to. Blank rows are skipped.

steps.title: Signing out clears this device.
steps.why: Projects and the migration marker are removed, so the next person sees none of it.

recap.title: Memory first, always
recap.body: Edits change the item in memory straight away. Saving follows.

recap.title: Typing is batched
recap.body: saveToStorageSoon waits a moment, so a burst of keys is one write.

recap.title: Two names for every field
recap.body: toTodoRowPayload maps tit / desc / due to title / description / due_date.

recap.title: Parents land first
recap.body: A todo write waits for its project's insert to finish.

steps.title: Each keystroke updates the item in memory.
steps.why: The title changes on the item right away. The save to disk is asked for, not done.

steps.title: Saves while typing are combined.
steps.why: One timer at a time: fast typing becomes a single write instead of one per key.

steps.title: All projects go to localStorage.
steps.why: The whole model is written under one key. Nothing else happens on a save.

steps.title: Memory names become column names.
steps.why: The app says tit, desc and due. The database says title, description and due_date.

steps.title: A todo waits for its project to exist.
steps.why: If the project's insert is still in flight, the todo write waits, so it's never orphaned.

steps.title: Insert or update, and note our own echo.
steps.why: New rows insert, edits update. noteSelfEcho lets realtime skip the copy we just sent.

recap.title: Realtime updates the data
recap.body: Supabase pushes each change; listLogic applies it to memory and storage.

recap.title: Re-sync repaints the screen
recap.body: hydrateFromSupabase pulls everything, then fires listLogicHydrated.

recap.title: Never while you type

recap.title: Server rows rebuild tasks
recap.body: A synced project takes its tasks from the server. Newer updated_at decides project fields only.

steps.title: Two live channels: projects and todos.
steps.why: Supabase pushes every insert, update and delete on those tables to this device.

steps.title: A pushed change is applied to memory.
steps.why: Our own echoes are skipped. Others are added, updated or removed, then saved locally.

steps.title: A full re-sync, but never while you type.
steps.why: Repainting would wipe a half-typed edit, so focus in an input skips this round.

steps.title: When re-syncs happen.
steps.why: Tab visible again, window focus or back online. A 5-minute timer is the backstop.

steps.title: Merge: server rows, pending inserts kept.
steps.why: Newer updated_at picks project fields only. Tasks come from server rows; local ones stay only while pending.

steps.why: Sidebar and list are rebuilt from the merged data, keeping the project you had open.

tours.title: When a save doesn't reach the server

recap.title: Fire-and-forget
recap.body: persistMutation logs a failed write and never tries it again.

recap.title: No session, no write
recap.body: Without a session the write stops before anything is sent.

recap.title: The server copy wins
recap.body: A synced project's tasks are rebuilt from server rows, so an unsent edit is replaced.

recap.body: An unconfirmed new task is carried over only while its id is in the in-memory pending set.

steps.title: An edit is sent to the server, not awaited.
steps.why: This follows a save that fails. Memory and localStorage already hold the edit; nothing on screen changes.

steps.title: A new task's id is noted as unconfirmed.
steps.why: Edits and deletes are not tracked here. The set is in memory only, so a reload empties it.

steps.title: No session: the write simply stops.
steps.why: Nothing is sent and nothing is queued. The change exists on this device only.

steps.title: A server error is logged, not retried.
steps.why: The warning goes to the console. Nothing rolls back the edit and nothing tries the write again.

steps.title: Back online triggers a full re-sync.
steps.why: This re-reads the server. It does not replay the write that failed.

steps.title: Tasks are rebuilt from the server's rows.
steps.why: A project on both sides takes its tasks' fields from server rows, so an edit that never arrived is replaced.

steps.title: Only pending inserts are carried over.
steps.why: A local-only task survives while its id is in the pending set. After a reload it is gone.

recap.title: Two channels, opened once
recap.body: Projects and todos each get a channel after sign-in.

recap.title: Four wake triggers
recap.body: Visible, online, focus and app-lock unlock each re-sync and reopen.

recap.title: Reopen is teardown plus subscribe
recap.body: Old channels are removed and the list emptied before subscribing again.

recap.title: The re-sync fills the gap

recap.title: Signed out is a no-op
recap.body: Without a session nothing is reopened.

steps.title: Two channels open once, after sign-in.
steps.why: This follows live updates dying and recovering. Calling this again while channels exist does nothing.

steps.title: Tab visible again: re-sync and reopen.
steps.why: A backgrounded phone or sleeping tab can drop the socket silently, with no error on screen.

steps.title: Online, focus and unlock run the same pair.
steps.why: Each wake trigger calls rehydrateUnlessEditing and wakeRecoverRealtime together.

steps.title: The wake hands off to listLogic.
steps.why: Any error is swallowed here; resubscribeToRealtime guards its own.

steps.title: Signed out? Nothing reopens.
steps.why: The flag is set when channels open after sign-in and cleared on sign-out.

steps.title: Old channels go, new ones open.
steps.why: The list is emptied first; otherwise subscribeToRealtime would return without reopening.

steps.title: The paired re-sync backfills the gap.
steps.why: Changes made while the socket was dead arrive here, unless you are typing in an input.

steps.why: Memory and localStorage change first; the delete request follows, not awaited.
